title: Content Definitions in Code: Migrations and Recipes | Orchard Core
description:
Content types, parts and fields built in the admin live in the database of one site. A module that needs them on every site has to define them in code.

Orchard Core offers two tools for that: a data migration, which alters content definitions through the content definition manager, and a recipe, which holds a longer definition as JSON and is run by a migration. The migration is versioned, so each site catches up on its own.

In this video:
• Why define content in code
• The migration class: manifest, registration and injection
• Content types: create and configure a type in C#
• Parts and fields: fields belong to parts
• Recipes: longer definitions as JSON
• Versions: every site catches up on its own
• A migration at work: the SEO module in the admin
• Reading the values in C#: a class for the part
